- **Valuation:** 11.9x trailing / **8.6x forward** vs healthcare sector 28.0/15.2. PEG 0.79. EPS $24.19 ttm → $33.49 fwd (+38% growth expected). FCF $8.0B on $76B cap = 10.5% yield. Dividend $6.24 (2.1%), covered 4x (25% payout).
- **Quality:** ROE 16.8%, revenue +6.7%, earnings +10.2%. Cash $7.3B vs debt $31.9B (D/E 74%).
- **Insider:** 14 buy transactions vs 5 sells in 6 months; net +14K shares. (Finviz 12-mo insider transactions −5.3% — mixed, but 6-mo tape is net positive.)
- **Analysts:** 25 covering, mean 1.72 (Buy), steady buys ~13-15 over 3 months. Target mean $339 / median $340.
- **Why:** Third straight week in the top 5 — cheapest large-cap managed-care/PBM franchise in the screen, with real earnings growth behind the low multiple. Current ratio 0.85 is typical for insurers (float business).
- **Risks:** PBM regulation (reform headlines), Express Scripts concentration, healthcare-cost trend. 65% of 52-week range — not beaten down, just cheap vs growth.

## Avoid — Screen Trap Warning

**MU (Micron) $927.60 — mcap ~$1.05T.** The screen screams "cheap" (5.9x fwd, PEG 0.14, ROE 67%, strong-buy consensus, target $1,513 = +63%) but this is the **classic cyclical peak trap**: revenue +346%, earnings +1,369% — peak-EPS multiples on memory cycles are historically where the multiple is most deceptive. Insiders sold −337K shares across 19 transactions (6-mo). A 5.9x P/E on *peak* HBM earnings is not Graham value; it's the same setup the screen flagged Aug 31, one step further along. Not a value pick — do not confuse a low multiple with a margin of safety here.

**Also distorted this week (trailing ≠ real):** HON 7.8x ttm vs 20.5x fwd (one-time gain), MKC 8.3x ttm vs 15.1x fwd, ALL 5.2x vs 9.3x, GM/GPN as noted. Rule of thumb from this screen: when trailing and forward P/E diverge >2x, one of them is lying — check which.

## Methodology
1. ~300-symbol large-cap universe (10 GICS-ish sectors) via Yahoo v7 quote API (real prices).
2. Sector-relative screen: P/E discount >5% vs sector median (trailing or forward, whichever is the larger positive gap) → 16-name shortlist.
3. Deep dive on 10 finalists: v10 quoteSummary (financialData, defaultKeyStatistics, summaryDetail, recommendationTrend, netSharePurchaseActivity) + Finviz insider stats.
4. Scored on: valuation discount, FCF yield, ROE, D/E, analyst mean/target, PEG, insider direction; qualitative overlay for earnings-quality distortions.

**Comparison vs prior runs:** CI and VICI are 3-for-3 since Aug 31 (CI $278→$289); VTRS 2nd appearance ($16.27→$16.65); FIS slid from ~$41 to a 52-week low $37.34 — thesis intact, conviction trimmed for leverage. MU dropped from the list per the cyclical-peak rule. New this week: GM enters top 5 on 28% FCF yield; ZM flagged for the screen's strongest insider buying.

*Educational screening only — not financial advice. Metrics are as-reported by Yahoo Finance/Finviz on Sep 15, 2026; trailing figures include one-time items flagged above. Verify primary filings before acting.*
